comparisons.reason: The single squat mint rectangular inset retains its width, height and central placement, with the same partial upper cap, bottom black slot and neighbor edges. Fine surface grain adds no frame, emblem, extra inset, halo or new directional highlight. The original teal-green surround and flatter brighter mint center remain the same material family.

The two main asymmetric mint lobes and the smaller left/top marks retain their number, tilted contours, relative spacing and dark diagonal separation. The horizontal ribbed neighbor on the left and partial top, right and lower architecture remain in their source positions. Surface grain does not turn the lobes into a symmetrical hourglass or a new glyph, and no glow spill or new light source appears.

The nearly flat dark-green plane retains its small disconnected black angular notches at left center and faint vertical value variation. The source remains quiet and dim: the fine grain does not create a crack, object, symbol, masonry pattern or illuminated feature. Exact black/STP classes support the preserved cutout positions.

The diagonal fan retains the original five unequal pointed folded lobes, their upper-left origin, overlapping value pattern, negative gaps and separate top/bottom neighboring pieces. Added shallow grain follows existing faces rather than adding a leaf, extra fold, cloth ornament or new tip. Its broad teal highlights and dark fold valleys remain source-led.

The eight unequal mint insets preserve their count, irregular sizes, centers and dark separations. The upper/side partial features and lower strip remain aligned. Fine surface texture retains the original flat insert identity without regularizing them into circles, a new tile grid or a decorative emblem, and there is no added halo or directional illumination.

Exactly two bent mint chevrons remain above the broad lower bright rectangle, with their original unequal angles, spacing and widths. The upper partial cap and segmented lower neighbors are preserved. Grain remains within those existing forms, without an extra chevron, sigil, branch, frame or new light source.

Both broad dark scalloped bowl-like lobes remain in their original stacked positions, with near-black interiors and the same sparse turquoise underside highlight groups. The left upright fragment and lower adjacent decorative pieces stay separate. The additional low-contrast surface grain does not fill the dark interiors or create an ornament or another lobe. Contrast is more defined than the coarse original, so native scale/seam review remains necessary, but the broad source lighting hierarchy is retained.

The tall central mint column, two small left bars, upper-left inset, irregular right upper marks and two lower-right bent chevrons all remain in the source positions. The count and dark separation of the bright forms are unchanged, as are the partial lower neighbors. Grain adds material definition without redesigning the panel as a rune or introducing glow.

The partial upper-left bent bands, single narrow right mint strip, its one black interruption and lower fragmented row remain aligned with the original. Fine grain resolves the dark teal face without adding joints, cracks, another notch, inset or decoration. The sparse composition and original bright-versus-dark relationship remain intact.

The two broad dim horizontal scalloped planes and their sparse turquoise underside highlight groups retain their relative heights and widths, with the upper partial fragments and right upright pale strip in the same places. Material grain follows the existing facets and keeps the broad planes dark; no new support, lobe, ornament or light source is introduced. The clearer facet edges require native-scale review but do not add a source-unsupported object.

The dim curved right rim keeps its bend and the four angled internal braces, with the same intersections, black margin and separate lower-left fragment. Fine grain sharpens the existing braces without inserting another member or inventing a mechanical symbol. The near-black teal illumination remains subdued rather than becoming a bright architectural feature.

The broad green face, tall plain left strip, existing pale right inset and its one diagonal dark channel remain in their source positions. The lower segmented scraps stay separate. Surface definition resolves the existing panel boundaries without an extra diagonal, pipe, tile grid, ornament or change in the underlying teal material identity; broad light/dark placement remains recognizable.

The broad plain dark-green central rectangle keeps the stepped top/left cutouts and disconnected lower angular pieces. The added grain is low contrast and continuous rather than a new motif, fissure, masonry joint or light patch. Dark field and adjoining strips remain in their original positions, with exact STP/black classes retaining the gaps.

The extremely dark lower plane, top thin fragments and faint vertical bars remain in their source positions. Fine texture stays subdued and does not turn the dark field into a recognizable wall, symbol, lit opening or new object. The broad near-black palette and partial left/top architecture are preserved.

The dark navy field retains exactly four unequal horizontal bars, their original spacing and rectangular orientation, plus the same partial top/side architecture. Fine grain does not add another bar or light source, and the original dim green-on-navy relationship remains intact.

The essentially flat pale cyan-white field retains its irregular perimeter, black notches, cuts and thin neighboring strips. The paper-like grain is fine and shallow; no cloud, directional beam, crack, emblem or additional light center appears. The broad pale field and soft lighter central area remain the same source material, rather than becoming a carved or faceted surface.

The upper partial curved cap, unequal small insert row, two broad stacked mint forms and narrow central stem preserve their original number and placements. The lower partial inset and surrounding fragments remain aligned. Fine grain defines existing material faces without introducing another glyph, frame or decorative joint; the brighter mint forms remain flat and the dark separation is retained.
